title: Review the year-end accrued liabilities schedule — Northfield Distributors
instructions: Northfield Distributors' staff accountant prepared the December 31 accrued liabilities schedule. Review each accrual against the source information. Tick every amount that is wrong and enter the correct amount.

exhibits.title: Source information
exhibits.content:
- **Payroll:** biweekly payroll is **$84,000** for 10 workdays, paid in arrears. The last payday was Friday, December 24, covering work through that date. December 27–31 are five workdays.
- **Term note:** **$600,000**, 6%, interest paid annually each **October 1** for the preceding 12 months. The October 1 payment was made on time.
- **Vacation:** employees have earned **$18,300** of vested, unused vacation at December 31.
- **Warranties:** products carry a one-year warranty. Expected cost is **2%** of sales. Sales for the year were **$2,400,000**. The warranty liability was **$11,000** on January 1, and warranty claims paid during the year were **$29,500**.
- **Utilities:** the December bill of **$6,200** arrived January 10.

rows.label: Accrued interest on the term note
rows.explanation: Interest was last paid October 1, so only October–December is unpaid: 600,000 × 6% × 3/12 = **9,000**. The staff accrued a full year.

rows.label: Accrued vacation pay
rows.explanation: Earned, vested, unused vacation is accrued when earned (ASC 710-10-25). **No error.**

rows.label: Warranty liability
rows.explanation: The liability is a roll-forward, not the year's expense: 11,000 + 48,000 − 29,500 claims paid = **29,500**.

rows.label: Accrued utilities
rows.explanation: December's usage, billed in January, is a December expense. **No error.**

parts.prompt: Compute the correct expense for the year.

rows.label: Warranty expense for the year
rows.explanation: 2,400,000 × 2% = **48,000**. The staff's 48,000 is the right *expense* but the wrong *liability*.

rows.label: Interest expense on the term note for the year
rows.explanation: Interest expense is always twelve months: 600,000 × 6% = **36,000**, whatever the payment dates. The October 1 payment settled the 9,000 accrued at last year-end plus 27,000 of this year's expense, and another 9,000 is accrued now.
